ivy: Heads-up bringing up halo-embed-v1 (1024d). After onnx int6-pertensor I'm seeing a systematic recall@10 gap on stack-exchange-sample and a few topic clusters shifting. Anyone seen a small-axes bias from quant before? :thinking:

noah: can you paste the eval command + quick numbers?

ivy: sure. Ran weekly slices (wk0..wk11). Command:

```
python eval_embed.py \n  --model halo-v1 \n  --quant onnx-int6 \n  --dataset stack-exchange-sample \n  --split weekly \n  --metrics recall@1,5,10,centroid_shift,dim_clip
```

Aggregated short summary:
- fp16: @1=0.534, @5=0.744, @10=0.812, centroid_shift=0.010, dim_clip=0.004
- int6-pertensor: @1=0.526, @5=0.732, @10=0.785, centroid_shift=0.017, dim_clip=0.028

anya: dim_clip jump is telling. Which dims clip?

ivy: dims ~[320..360] show heavy clipping and also higher variance in fp16. Seems topic-specific (these dims encode programming vs ops topics).

ravi: two quick experiments: (1) int6-perchannel calibration on a stratified topic sample, (2) low-rank correction: learn a rank-1 vector r so that int6_emb + alpha*r aligns with fp16 mean on calibration pairs. Cheap to apply at index-time.

ivy: queued a calibration job and a rank-1 fit. mlbot: eval job queued.

mlbot: eval-bot: job 71021 queued by ivy (int6-perchannel calibration + rank1-fit).

noah: also try ensemble ordering if you used multi-ckpt. avg->quant tends to reduce per-dim clipping vs quant->avg.

ivy: single ckpt for now. Quick interim from calibration (18m): int6-perchannel @10 -> 0.797, centroid_shift -> 0.012, dim_clip -> 0.011. Rank-1 fit (alpha optimized on calib) further @10 -> 0.803.

ravi: nice. Does the rank-1 correction generalize across weeks and topics, or overfits to calib?

ivy: tested on 3 heldout weeks: average +0.012 rec@10 vs raw int6, small variance. Topic-level checks: programming cluster improved +0.04 @10, other clusters unchanged.

anya: what's the rank-1 compute? Simple least-squares on paired means? Can you share snippet?

ivy: snippet used:
```
# X=int6_embs, Y=fp16_embs (calib pairs)
r = mean(Y - X, axis=0)
alpha = argmin_alpha || mean((X + alpha*r) - Y)||_2 // closed-form
# apply: X_corrected = X + alpha*r at index time
```

noah: that's basically a directional bias correction. Low compute and easy to store. Watch for sign flips across domains.

mlbot: job 71021 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/halo/v1/onboard/4291002345/job-71021/

infra-bot: infra note: staging used onnxrt 1.16 with CUDA 12.1. Confirm prod parity before promoting.

ivy: confirmed prod parity planned. Also tried HNSW tweaks: ef_construction=300 + ef_search=180 recovered another +0.003 rec@10 for corrected int6. Latency bump acceptable for non-SLA tiers.

ravi: recommended onboarding checklist additions if stable: 1) int6-perchannel calibration stratified by topic, 2) dim-clip diagnostic, 3) rank-1 directional correction opt-in at index-time, 4) HNSW ef guidance, 5) ensemble advice (avg->quant).

anya: I'll draft a small PR with the calibration + rank1 scripts and the eval dashboard snapshots. Ivy, please drop the job ids and plots in the ticket.

ivy: will do. Final note: rank-1 correction reduced centroid_shift nearly to fp16 levels and rec@10 gap is ~0.004 now. We'll run a 2-week rolling check then decide. Thanks for the quick eyes. :raised_hands:
